title: Μελισσουργός
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 235. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Εἰς μελισσουργοῦ τις εἰσελθών, ἐκείνου ἀπόντος, τό τε μέλι καὶ τὰ κηρία ὑφείλετο.
sentences.tr: Eis melissourgou tis eiselthōn, ekeinou apontos, to te meli kai ta kēria hypheileto.
sentences.l: Someone, having gone into a beekeeper's, that man being away, stole both the honey and the combs.
sentences.i: A man went into a beekeeper's while the owner was away, and made off with both the honey and the combs.
sentences.n: εἰς μελισσουργοῦ leaves the noun for 'house' unsaid after the genitive — Greek does this as freely as English says 'at the doctor's'. ὑφαιρέομαι in the middle is to take away from under someone, i.e. to filch.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ ἐπανελθών, ἐπειδὴ ἐθεάσατο ἐρήμους τὰς κυψέλας, εἱστήκει ταύτας διερευνῶν.
sentences.tr: Ho de epanelthōn, epeidē etheasato erēmous tas kypselas, heistēkei tautas diereunōn.
sentences.l: And he, having returned, when he beheld the hives empty, stood searching them through.
sentences.n: ὁ δέ with no noun after it marks the change of subject: the thief has had his sentence, and this is the beekeeper. εἱστήκει is the pluperfect of ἵστημι, and this verb's perfect means simply 'stand', so the pluperfect means 'was standing'. ἐρήμους is predicative: he saw the hives as empty, which is the seeing that matters.

sentences.t: Αἱ δὲ μέλισσαι ἐπανελθοῦσαι ἀπὸ τῆς νομῆς, ὡς κατέλαβον αὐτόν, παίουσαι τοῖς κέντροις, τὰ πάνδεινα διετίθεσαν.
sentences.tr: Hai de melissai epanelthousai apo tēs nomēs, hōs katelabon auton, paiousai tois kentrois, ta pandeina dietithesan.
sentences.l: And the bees, having returned from their foraging, when they came upon him, striking with their stings, were treating him most dreadfully.
sentences.i: And the bees came back from their foraging, and when they found him there they set on him with their stings and used him most cruelly.
sentences.n: διατίθημι with an accusative like τὰ πάνδεινα means to put someone in a state — here the worst state of all — and the imperfect keeps it going: they went on at him. νομή is the grazing-ground, used of bees for their range of flowers.

sentences.t: Κἀκεῖνος ἔφη πρὸς αὐτάς· « Ὦ κάκιστα ζῷα, ὑμεῖς τὸν μὲν κλέψαντα ὑμῶν τὰ κηρία ἀθῷον ἀφήκατε, ἐμὲ δὲ τὸν ἐπιμελούμενον ὑμῶν δεινῶς τύπτετε. »
sentences.tr: Kakeinos ephē pros autas· « Ō kakista zōia, hymeis ton men klepsanta hymōn ta kēria athōion aphēkate, eme de ton epimeloumenon hymōn deinōs typtete. »
sentences.l: And he said to them: « O most wicked creatures, you let go unpunished the one who stole your combs, but me, the one who cares for you, you strike terribly. »
sentences.i: And he said to them: « You vile creatures, you have let the man who stole your combs go scot-free, and me, who look after you, you sting without mercy. »
sentences.n: Κἀκεῖνος is καὶ ἐκεῖνος run together by crasis. The μέν … δέ pair sets the thief against the keeper, and the two articular participles, τὸν κλέψαντα and τὸν ἐπιμελούμενον, are the whole of the injustice. ἀθῷος is 'unpunished', literally free of the penalty.

sentences.t: Οὕτως ἔνιοι τῶν ἀνθρώπων δι’ ἄγνοιαν τοὺς ἐχθροὺς μὴ φυλαττόμενοι, τοὺς φίλους ὡς ἐπιβούλους ἀπωθοῦνται.
sentences.tr: Houtōs enioi tōn anthrōpōn di’ agnoian tous echthrous mē phylattomenoi, tous philous hōs epiboulous apōthountai.
sentences.l: So some among men, through ignorance not guarding against their enemies, thrust away their friends as plotters.
sentences.i: So some men, through ignorance failing to guard against their enemies, push their friends away as though they were the plotters.
sentences.n: φυλάττομαι in the middle with the accusative is to be on one's guard against someone; ὡς with ἐπιβούλους gives the character wrongly assigned — treated 'as being' plotters.
